metadata.title: Exact Non-Perturbative Spectral Mass Gap, Complete Glueball Spectrum, and Center Vortex Condensation for SU(3) Yang-Mills Theory on 3D Voronoi-Delaunay Space in Unified Phase Dynamics
metadata.description:
We construct a non-perturbative mathematical framework establishing the rigorous existence of quantum Yang–Mills theory with compact gauge group G = SU(3) on strictly three-dimensional physical space ℝ3 discretized by a Poisson–Delaunay triangulation and its circumcentric Voronoi dual with exact analytical mean coordination number ⟨z3D⟩ = 48π2/35 + 2 ≈ 15.5355, where time emerges solely as the continuous parameter of unitary quantum phase evolution generated by the Hamiltonian operator along the 4-vector phase current.

Discretizing the pure-color projection of the universal master-functional Ψ[Σ] via circumcentric Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC) with discrete Hodge star weights eliminates unphysical cubic lattice artifacts and restores continuous SO(4) rotational symmetry in the continuum limit. Because physical space is three-dimensional and time enters through the continuous contraction semigroup on a positive-definite Haar measure space, the construction trivially satisfies strict Osterwalder–Seiler reflection positivity (OS2) for all cutoffs a > 0, completely avoiding Lee–Wick ghost poles and Schoenberg–Bochner oscillations.

Under block-spin renormalization-group decimation, thick center Z3 vortices condense on dual 2-cells, generating the fundamental string tension σ ≈ (440 MeV)2. Applying the Glimm–Jaffe–Simon chessboard bound with the Borel–Chebyshev inequality proves a strictly positive spectral mass gap Δ ≥ √(6/π)√σ ≈ 608.1 MeV > 0, and the complete glueball spectrum with ground state scalar glueball mass Δ0++ = ℏc ΛYM C(SU(3)) ≈ 1.65–1.68 GeV matching Lattice QCD. In the flat-space limit G → 0, the proof is fully autonomous without gravitons, while embedded into the cosmological master-functional, the 19-order hierarchy ΛYM/MPl ≈ 1.8 × 10−20 is deduced from SU(3) asymptotic freedom.
